newsitem.title: UK: UK television regulator issues warning to Live TV.
newsitem.headline: UK television regulator issues warning to Live TV.

text.p: Britain's television watchdog said on Wednesday that it had issued formal warnings to cable channel Live TV and to satellite television station MED TV for breaching codes regulating broadcasts.
The Independent Television Commission (ITC) said it issued the warning to Live TV, part of Mirror Group Newspapers Plc, for repeated compliance failures.

The ITC said Live TV gave "undue prominence" to the Daily Mirror, one of the newspapers owned by Mirror Group, in a news item on the Duchess of York and in its broadcast of "The Princess Diana Hoax Special", which was shown repeatedly over two days.

Live TV's "Princess Diana Hoax Special" followed the publication by the Sun, a tabloid newspaper owned by Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd, of photographs which it had alleged showed Princess Diana cavorting with former lover James Hewitt. The Sun one day later admitted the photos, taken from a video, were a hoax, and it issued a front-page apology.

The ITC, separately, said it was seeking clarification from Sky News about aspects of its coverage of the hoax Diana tape. Sky News is part of satellite broadcaster British Sky Broadcasting, which is 40 percent owned by News Corp.

The ITC said Live TV also breached its code on sponsorship and advertising breaks on September 24, when all programmes were sponsored by Cadbury's Fuse. The ITC said it was unclear whether the announcements, "This is Fuseday on Live TV," were advertisements, sponsorship credits or station continuity announcements.
The ITC said it had lodged four code breaches against Live TV over the past year.

In issuing a formal warning to MED TV, which provides a service to Kurdish viewers in Europe, Turkey and the Middle East, the ITC said station had breached the code for impartiality on matters of political controversy.
The ITC said it imposed the formal warning after continuing problems in securing compliance from MED TV following an intervention on impartiality and coverage of the Turkish elections last March.
